propositions: Completion verification currently materializes the full ticket store despite reading only a small subset, causing 135-235 seconds of close latency that can be reduced by lazy pinned reads to ~29ms per ticket.
Close publishes PASS COMPLETION_VERDICT, STATUS transition, and completion SIGNATURE through separate writes, creating durability windows where partial updates survive failures.

The new design must pin tickets_oid and code_oid once at operation start, resolve all ticket queries against the pinned state without live fallback, and record negative reads and full dependency receipts.

Close atomicity requires one committed-store transaction containing all three events (PASS sidecar, closed STATUS, completion SIGNATURE) or none, with rollback restoring prior HEAD/index/worktree on any fault.

Prevalidation must check that the receipt from initial state A reaches current state Tn without ancestor violations, and recompute affected predicates to detect hierarchy, link, resolver, or negative-read conflicts that invalidate the verdict.

Parallel close attempts must serialize: one wins with all three events; the loser recognizes an equivalent close or restarts without leaving partial artifacts, while unrelated concurrent mutations revalidate and retry independently.
